item.title: Why x̄
item.description:
A short on the name, teaching goals, and this tiny lab.

The Name

x̄ (x-bar) represents the sample mean in statistics — the average of a sample drawn from a population. It’s one of the most fundamental concepts in statistical inference, bridging the gap between what we observe and what we can infer about the world.

Teaching Goals

This project aims to make statistical concepts more intuitive through interactive visualization. Rather than just showing formulas, we want students to see and feel how sampling distributions emerge, how confidence intervals behave, and why p-values work the way they do.

item.title: Design Notes
item.description:
Color, spacing, and motion choices for clarity and calm.

Color Palette

The XBAR color system uses a minimal palette designed for high contrast and accessibility:

  • Ink (#001524): Primary text color, ensuring maximum readability
  • Navy (#15616D): Primary accent for parameter lines and UI elements
  • Orange (#FF7D00): Call-to-action color and active states
  • Info (#475569): Secondary text for metadata and descriptions

Typography

Inter for body text provides excellent readability at all sizes, while JetBrains Mono adds subtle coding references without overwhelming the design.
